scope: Exact Ubuntu systemd259.5-0ubuntu3.4 plus glibc2.43-2ubuntu2.4 on Image-v9. Read-only source and binary audit; no kernel patch, package replacement or device change.

qemu_observation.label: ubuntu26-kernel9-systemd
qemu_observation.exact_failure: leon-audit.service: Failed to spawn executor: Function not implemented
qemu_observation.note: The log prints the planned ExecStart command containing LAB_SYSTEMD_SERVICE_STARTED. That occurrence is not proof the service executed; subsequent spawn failure proves it did not.

conclusion.observed: The manager reaches service scheduling, but cannot spawn systemd-executor. This is a concrete service-start failure rather than merely a documented old-kernel warning.
conclusion.source_attribution: Confirmed by a PID1-preserving syscall trace: raw waitid(P_PIDFD, INT_MAX, NULL, WEXITED|WNOHANG) returns EINVAL on kernel9. glibc pidfd_spawn caches that capability as unsupported and returns ENOSYS before attempting clone3 for the executor.
conclusion.confidence: Direct syscall trace plus exact Ubuntu glibc/systemd source and actual binary imports agree.
conclusion.not_pidfd_open_only: pidfd_open is a separate missing API and will matter elsewhere, but it is not the direct syscall used by this pidfd_spawn capability gate. Implementing pidfd_open alone cannot fix this service spawn.
conclusion.not_clone3_unconditionally: For pidfd_spawn without POSIX_SPAWN_SETCGROUP, glibc2.43 can fall back from clone3 to legacy clone(CLONE_PIDFD). systemd retries without the SETCGROUP flag. Therefore clone3 itself is not unconditionally required for this specific executor path; complete usable pidfd semantics are required.

actual_binary.finding: Official libsystemd-shared-259.so imports pidfd_spawn@GLIBC_2.39 and uses its compiled HAVE_PIDFD_SPAWN path. No ordinary posix_spawn import was found in this binary.

call_chain.behavior: exec_spawn serializes the service invocation and calls posix_spawn_wrapper for the pinned systemd-executor file descriptor. A negative result is logged as Failed to spawn executor.

The HAVE_PIDFD_SPAWN build first requests POSIX_SPAWN_SETCGROUP. Supported errors trigger one retry after clearing SETCGROUP; that retry still calls pidfd_spawn. The ordinary posix_spawn branch is compile-time #else, not a runtime ENOSYS fallback.

If SPAWN_XFLAGS_RET_PIDFD is set, __clone_pidfd_supported() is evaluated first. Failure returns positive ENOSYS directly. After that gate, clone3 gets CLONE_PIDFD, CLONE_VM, CLONE_VFORK, CLONE_CLEAR_SIGHAND and optional CLONE_INTO_CGROUP. On ENOSYS/EINVAL and no SETCGROUP, legacy clone fallback remains available.

Capability detection issues raw waitid with P_PIDFD and an intentionally impossible descriptor INT_MAX. Only EBADF means pidfd wait is supported; EINVAL caches unsupported. This is not pidfd_open, and it occurs before spawning a helper child.
kernel_waitid accepts P_ALL, P_PID and P_PGID only. Other which values, including P_PIDFD, return EINVAL. Kernel9 time64 changes do not add P_PIDFD.
The legacy fallback forwards the low clone flags and pidfd return pointer through parent_tid. It requires genuine legacy clone(CLONE_PIDFD) support, which current kernel9 does not provide.

Other pidref_set_pid paths use pidfd_open and only tolerate resource-exhaustion fallback. ENOSYS is not accepted. This is an additional compatibility requirement, separate from the first executor failure.

requirements_to_fix_properly: Do not change only the waitid error to EBADF or fake the feature probe. That would bypass glibc protection while legacy kernel clone may ignore unsupported CLONE_PIDFD and fail to return a real descriptor. The entire pidfd object/lifetime/wait semantics must be implemented first.
Backport real pollable pidfd lifetime/reference semantics and kernel9 ABI-preserving structure integration, not just syscall numbers.
Provide waitid(P_PIDFD) with valid descriptor lookup, correct EBADF/EINVAL behavior, child ownership checks, WNOHANG/WNOWAIT and exit/reap semantics.
Provide safe CLONE_PIDFD through legacy clone or fully implemented clone3; test CLOEXEC, parent_tid interactions, child creation failures and file descriptor cleanup.
Add pidfd_open and pidfd_send_signal for manager lifecycle paths and verify PID-reuse safety, permissions and process exit behavior.
CLONE_INTO_CGROUP can remain unsupported for initial executor bring-up because systemd259 retries without it; do not pretend that this covers resource-control/sandbox feature completeness.
Retest the actual Ubuntu service, executor, restart/reexec and child reaping after each backport; subsequent API gaps may appear after this first failure.

verification_plan.read_only_probe: Run raw waitid(P_PIDFD, INT_MAX, NULL, WEXITED|WNOHANG) in a disposable kernel9 QEMU guest: expected current errno EINVAL; a real supported implementation should return EBADF for this invalid descriptor.
verification_plan.glibc_probe: Using exact Ubuntu glibc, call pidfd_spawn on a harmless /bin/true first with no cgroup flag, then with a dedicated cgroup and the same retry behavior as systemd. Record the function return value (positive errno), not only global errno.
verification_plan.trace: Completed in ubuntu26-kernel9-systemd-trace. PID1 waitid capability gate returned EINVAL, and no clone3/clone/execve follows this gate before the audit watchdog powers off.
verification_plan.negative_control: Ordinary posix_spawn on /bin/true should be tested independently to show that generic process creation works while pidfd_spawn does not.
verification_plan.post_fix: Require successful helper execution, poll/close/waitid on returned pidfd, no leaked child or fd, and LAB_SYSTEMD_SERVICE_STARTED emitted by the actual child rather than the debug command line.

version_distinctions: Ubuntu26.04 ships systemd259.5 here, not262. Exact259.5 minimum supported kernel is5.4, recommended5.7.

259.5 keeps mountpoint fallback without STATX_ATTR_MOUNT_ROOT and probes optional cgroup mount flags; kernel9 manager boot demonstrates those older-kernel fallbacks operate far enough to reach service spawning.
The glibc package overall supports older kernels, but optional APIs such as pidfd_spawn require kernel features newer than that general libc baseline.
The waitid capability gate failure is now directly observed in the PID1 syscall trace, not only inferred from source.

trace_observation.label: ubuntu26-kernel9-systemd-trace
trace_observation.actual_failure_confirmed: PID1 raw waitid(P_PIDFD, INT_MAX, NULL, WNOHANG|WEXITED, ...) returned EINVAL; the manager reports pidfd_spawn executor failure ENOSYS.
trace_observation.interpretation: The pidfd capability gate blocks this executor path before any subsequent clone3/clone or executor execve. Earlier generator forks are unrelated.
